prompt: Art direction: an original texture for a small, low-poly, early-2000s freeware PC first-person shooter. The look is a modest, slightly painterly, photo-sourced game texture of that era: low resolution in feel, soft detail, mild noise and grain, no ultra-sharp micro-detail, no modern PBR or hyper-realistic rendering. Palette: muted and slightly desaturated, earthy and industrial greys, browns, olives, dull reds and blues; no neon, no saturated rainbow colours. Lighting: flat, even and neutral, as if shot under an overcast sky; no strong baked shadows, no highlights or specular glare, no directional light gradient, no vignette, no ambient-occlusion darkening at the borders. Content rules: absolutely no text, letters, numbers, signage, logos, symbols, watermarks, signatures, brand names or trademarks of any kind. No people, no faces. The design must be wholly original and must not imitate any existing game, film or product. Subject: a square, seamlessly tileable surface texture of a weathered grey cast-concrete compound wall, faint formwork lines and light water staining spread evenly, seamless for 8x repeats along a wide wall. Requirements: - It MUST tile seamlessly on all four sides: the left edge continues exactly into the right edge and the top edge continues exactly into the bottom edge, with no visible seam, border, frame, margin or edge darkening when repeated in a grid. - Straight-on orthographic view, perfectly flat to the camera; no perspective, no foreshortening, no horizon, no depth of field. - Detail, wear and colour variation are evenly distributed across the whole image; no single focal point, no unique feature that would stand out when repeated, no large stains concentrated in one area. - Uniform brightness from corner to corner; no vignette, no gradient, no spotlight, no cast shadows. - The texture fills the entire square canvas edge to edge; it is a texture swatch only, not a scene, not an object on a background, not a mockup.
